idiom_name: none - object layout belongs to the engine (Smi tagging, packed elements); TypedArray/DataView for packed records
alternative: Leave small-value layout to the engine and keep objects monomorphic with packed elements and small integers in Smi range; use TypedArray/DataView over an ArrayBuffer when values must be packed densely, and reuse buffers instead of hand-rolling union encodings, which the just-in-time compiler cannot optimize.
implementation_notes: JavaScript exposes no object layout: a program cannot declare an inline buffer inside an object, and the engine already performs the analogous optimization where it can - in V8's pointer-compressed representation a tagged value holds either a pointer or 'a small integer ... without having to allocate additional storage for it' (Smi), and element storage has its own packed/double/object kinds. What a program does control is shape and density: monomorphic objects that keep their hidden class, arrays that stay packed, numbers that stay in Smi range, and TypedArrays when records must be packed without per-value wrappers. Hand-rolled union objects (a {tag, a, b} bag, or payloads encoded into strings and numbers) fight the engine's assumptions, create megamorphic access paths and usually lose against simply allocating the small object, so treat the classic structure as unavailable and optimize allocation count and shapes instead.
pitfalls: Hidden-class discipline is the real lever: adding properties after construction, mixing shapes, using delete or storing unlike values in one array makes access megamorphic and can cost far more than the allocation the union encoding tried to avoid.

Smi range and boxing are engine details: exceed the small-integer range, store the number in an object property that gets boxed, or use BigInt and the value becomes a heap object, so 'small integers are free' is not a language guarantee and varies by engine and version.

DataView/TypedArray storage is outside the garbage collector's object graph: offsets, endianness and bounds are now the program's responsibility, and a detached or resized ArrayBuffer silently empties the view.
sources: V8 blog, Pointer Compression in V8 - in the compressed representation a tagged value is either a pointer or a small integer: 'the value of an integer can be stored directly in the tagged value, without having to allocate additional storage for it': https://v8.dev/blog/pointer-compression

MDN Web Docs, TypedArray - typed arrays are array-like views over a binary ArrayBuffer with fixed element widths, the dense alternative to per-value objects: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/TypedArray
